title: Spring @Transactional Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes on Spring @Transactional: the proxy mental model, propagation, isolation, rollback rules, readOnly, self-invocation and boundary design, ending with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Transactions and the Proxy Mental Model
points: @Transactional works via an AOP proxy: the caller hits the proxy, which begins the transaction, calls your bean, then commits or rolls back
Transaction is bound to the current thread (ThreadLocal) and one Connection; new threads or @Async calls do NOT join it
Default behavior: propagation REQUIRED, isolation DEFAULT (the DB's own level), rollback only on unchecked exceptions
Only public methods on Spring-managed beans are proxied; private, final or static methods silently get no transaction
Put @Transactional on the service layer, not controllers or repositories: the service method is the unit of work

chapters.title: Propagation: REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW, NESTED
points: REQUIRED (default): join the existing transaction, or start one if none exists; inner failure marks the whole transaction rollback-only
REQUIRES_NEW: suspend the outer transaction and run on a new connection with an independent commit/rollback; used for audit logs
NESTED: a savepoint inside the outer transaction; inner rollback goes back to the savepoint only, but outer rollback undoes everything (needs JDBC savepoints, not JPA-only setups)
Gotcha: REQUIRES_NEW holds two connections at once, so it can exhaust the pool and deadlock if the outer transaction locks rows the inner one needs
Others: SUPPORTS (join if present, else none), MANDATORY (throw if none), NOT_SUPPORTED (suspend, run without), NEVER (throw if one exists)

chapters.title: Isolation Levels
points: READ_UNCOMMITTED allows dirty reads; READ_COMMITTED blocks dirty reads but allows non-repeatable reads
REPEATABLE_READ blocks non-repeatable reads; phantom reads are still possible by the SQL standard (MySQL InnoDB largely prevents them)
SERIALIZABLE prevents all anomalies at the cost of locking or retries and the lowest throughput
Set per method: @Transactional(isolation = Isolation.READ_COMMITTED); DEFAULT uses the database level (PostgreSQL: READ_COMMITTED, MySQL: REPEATABLE_READ)
Isolation applies only when a NEW transaction starts; a method joining an existing one (REQUIRED) ignores its own isolation setting

chapters.title: Rollback Rules and readOnly
points: Default: rollback on RuntimeException and Error; a checked exception (IOException, custom Exception) COMMITS
Override with rollbackFor = Exception.class, or noRollbackFor = SomeException.class to keep the commit
Catching an exception inside the method hides it from the proxy, so the transaction commits; rethrow to roll back
If an inner REQUIRED method throws and the outer catches it, the commit fails with UnexpectedRollbackException because the transaction is already rollback-only
readOnly = true is a hint: Hibernate skips dirty checking/flush and the driver may route to a replica; it does not stop writes on every database

chapters.title: Self-Invocation and Transaction Boundaries
points: this.otherMethod() bypasses the proxy, so @Transactional on otherMethod is ignored (same for REQUIRES_NEW)
Fixes: move the method to another bean (preferred), inject self or use AopContext.currentProxy(), or use TransactionTemplate programmatically
Keep transactions short: never make remote HTTP calls or slow I/O inside one, since the connection and locks stay held
LazyInitializationException occurs when lazy entities are touched after the transaction ends; fetch inside the service or use DTOs
Side effects such as emails or messages should run after commit with @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT), or they fire for a transaction that later rolls back

chapters.title: @Transactional Cheat Sheet
points: Propagation: REQUIRED joins or creates; REQUIRES_NEW suspends and starts independent; NESTED uses a savepoint
Isolation ladder: READ_UNCOMMITTED (dirty) < READ_COMMITTED < REPEATABLE_READ < SERIALIZABLE; each level blocks one more anomaly
Rollback: unchecked and Error roll back, checked commits; fix with rollbackFor = Exception.class
Silent no-ops: self-invocation, private or final methods, non-Spring-managed objects, catching the exception
Checklist: public service method, short transaction, readOnly for queries, side effects after commit
